answer: Yes, moderately. Of 159 USGS Ida high-water marks, 51% sat in a 2 m bare-earth DEM sink deeper than 0.15 m versus 12% of 3,180 random control points within 500 m (20 per mark). TPI (102 m window) was below local mean at 79% of marks vs 51% of controls. Paired per mark against its own controls, marks sat more sink-like 74.5% of the time (AUC 0.745, bootstrap 95% CI 0.71-0.78); TPI AUC 0.72. Excluding 31 interior-flagged marks gives 0.73; good/excellent-quality marks 0.82. Deeper marks sit in deeper sinks (Spearman 0.39, n=152). Marks are also lower in absolute elevation than neighbours (median 8.5 vs 12.0 m), so part of the signal is simply low ground. This shows association, not that a terrain-only model predicts flooding: controls are not verified dry and sewer backup is unmodelled.
traps_or_caveats: CSV line 1 is a citation; header parsed from line 2 (read_marks uses header_line=1).
HWM heights are feet; converted to meters (x0.3048) to compare with metric 3DEP; sink and TPI are in meters. Only used for the depth correlation.

Presence-only: marks exist only where flooding was surveyed, so controls (random points within 500 m, seed 7, water/<0.5 m elevation skipped) are assumed not-flooded but are unverified; true hit/false-alarm rates cannot be computed.
31 marks have interior/basement-type wording in their descriptions (keyword flag); results reported with and without them (AUC 0.745 vs 0.73), and interior depths are measured from interior floors.
Bare-earth DEM omits sewers, buildings, curbs and drainage, so sewer-backup or building-edge flooding is not captured; a sink on the DEM is not proof water ponds there.

Marks were surveyed where USGS crews looked (survey-selection bias, spatially clustered, often on structures), so the 159 are not a random sample of flooded places; the bootstrap CI treats marks as independent and is likely too narrow.

Part of the signal is absolute elevation (marks sit in lower ground than neighbours); the 500 m control radius mixes this with micro-topography. The result is an association with 2 m terrain, not causal proof.
Mark positions are phone/vehicle GPS; 2 m cell values at a mark can differ from the true surveyed spot; TPI near tile edges may be edge-affected (marks preferentially picked tiles with 60 m margin).
Score My Layer was not run: this is a descriptive terrain-vs-observed comparison, not a scored prediction layer.
